extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers of English literature interested in John Bunyan and religious allegory
extracted.subtask_description: Critical assessment of John Bunyan's imaginative works (Pilgrim's Progress, Life of Mr. Badman, poems) emphasizing what makes effective allegory, prose, and devotional poetry. Focuses on qualities such as universality, sympathy with character, economy of language, and faithfulness to spiritual truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature as means of teaching spiritual truth
rubrics_metrics.description: He cared simply for spiritual truth, and literature in his eyes was only useful as a means of teaching it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author treats literary form instrumentally: the primary aim is to convey spiritual/doctrinal truth and to make others understand religious doctrine and practice. Works should be judged by their effectiveness at teaching and clarifying faith, not by mere aesthetic novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy with characters; painting characters as they see themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: Every character, if justice is to be done to it, must be painted at its best, as it appears to itself; ... Bunyan, intensely religious as he was, and narrow as his theology was, is always human.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective characterization requires sympathy and the ability to present figures from their own perspective; even a writer with narrow doctrine should aim to render characters as rounded, self-consistent persons rather than caricatures. This yields humane and believable portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality / large spirit of humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Pilgrim's Progress,' though professedly an allegoric story of the Protestant plan of salvation, is conceived in the large, wide spirit of humanity itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful religious allegory attains themes and shapes that transcend sectarian limits so readers of various creeds and ages can find themselves in it. Assess works for cross-denominational appeal and the ability to reflect common human experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelessness and staying power
rubrics_metrics.description: Time cannot impair its interest, or intellectual progress make it cease to be true to experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge works by their durability: whether they retain interest and relevance across generations, surviving the decay of contemporary theological tracts to enter common memory and childhood reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegory as an intrinsically valuable imaginative form
rubrics_metrics.description: His especial gift was for allegory, the single form of imaginative fiction which he would not have considered trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegory should be treated as a major imaginative form capable of serious literature. Evaluate the work's success in using allegory to convey moral and spiritual meanings without becoming lifeless abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain, unaffected Saxon prose as an instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: His especial instrument was plain, unaffected Saxon prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity and simplicity of diction (plain Saxon words) are virtues in devotional and allegorical writing: plain speech serves doctrinal clarity and emotional directness. Assess prose for its directness and lack of unnecessary ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance over ornament in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: No verse is doggerel which has a sincere and rational meaning in it. Goethe... says that the test of poetry is the substance which remains when the poetry is reduced to prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate poetry primarily by its substantive meaning and rational sincerity; if the core content survives conversion to prose, it indicates real poetic worth rather than mere surface prettiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and precision of language; rhythmic prose
rubrics_metrics.description: He could express what he wished with sharp, defined outlines, and without the waste of a word. The rhythmical structure of his prose is carefully correct. Scarcely a syllable is ever out of place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prose for economy (no wasted words), precise expression, and an internal rhythm that makes prose nearly musical. Such economy and rhythm contribute to clarity and memorability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorability through fitting poetic form
rubrics_metrics.description: If one of the motives of poetical form be to clothe thought and feeling in the dress in which it can lie most easily remembered, Bunyan's lines are often as successful as the best lines of Quarles or George Herbert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetic form should serve memory and the content: judge verse by how well the form aids recollection and matches the thought and feeling it expresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness and clarity in biblical adaptation/translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The prose of the translation in the English Bible, faultless as it is, loses nothing in Bunyan's hands... if we found these poems in the collected works of a poet laureate, we should consider that a difficult task had been accomplished successfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting or translating sacred texts, preserve exact meaning and original grace without superfluous ornament; clarity and fidelity to the source are marks of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding literary work in human life and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: His real study was human life as he had seen it, and the human heart as he had experienced the workings of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good imaginative writing springs from careful observation of real life and psychological experience. Evaluate the extent to which the author draws on lived experience to inform believable motives and situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concreteness of allegorical types
rubrics_metrics.description: The figures stand for typical characters; but ... Bunyan's shadows are solid men whom we can feel and handle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegorical figures should be rendered with tangible individuality so that typological roles do not lapse into mere abstractions; successful allegory combines typicity with vivid concreteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Didactic narrative should show opportunities and moral consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: He wished to represent the good-for-nothing character, under the more instructive aspect of worldly success, which bad men may arrive at as well as good, if they are prudent and cunning. Bunyan gives his hero every chance... he creates opportunities for repentance at every stage of a long career—opportunities which the reprobate nature cannot profit by, yet increases its guilt by neglecting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In moral or didactic tales, narratively present repeated chances for repentance and the character's failures; this instructive structure shows moral culpability and enhances the lesson's force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solitude and leisure as conditions for higher literary work
rubrics_metrics.description: The periods of calm enabled him to discover powers in himself of which he might otherwise have never known the existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that intervals of silence, reflection, and removal from constant speaking or activity can foster deeper imaginative and intellectual development; the writer's environment and time for reflection contribute to quality.
